svg.text: Step steer 1° at 20 m/s. Rise time 194 ms, overshoot 1%, damping ratio 0.98.
A · Yaw rate against closed-form theory
B · The same input at three inertias
more inertia: slower AND more overshoot
C · What we do not know about Izz

Panel A is the check that matters: the measured response and the closed-form second-order solution are the same curve, and none of that theory appears in our code. Panel C is the caveat — the three published ways to estimate yaw inertia disagree by 36%, which is 62 ms of rise time. Report the direction of the inertia effect confidently and its magnitude loosely.

[MEASURED] bicycle model + Sedan_Pac02Tire.tir · offsets removed · m 1360 kg · Izz 1950 kg·m² · 54% front · [SOURCED] RV-1 parameters, vehicle-reference-parameters.md §1 · Izz correlations [SOURCED] vehicle-reference-parameters.md §1
Rise time is 10-90% of final yaw rate; overshoot is peak over final. Final value is the mean of the last 10% of the trace, so a decaying tail does not distort every metric.
